title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 94 (Place of keeping and inspection of registers)

content.overview: Section 94 governs where section 88 registers and copies of the section 92 annual return are kept and how they may be inspected. It sets the conditions for an alternative location, distinguishes inspection rights and fees, restricts prescribed personal particulars, and provides a continuing-default penalty and a Central Government remedy.
content.glance: Section 94 governs where section 88 registers and copies of the section 92 annual return are kept and how they may be inspected. It sets the conditions for an alternative location, distinguishes inspection rights and fees, restricts prescribed personal particulars, and provides a continuing-default penalty and a Central Government remedy.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 94 (Place of keeping and inspection of registers, returns, etc.). Registers required under section 88 and copies of the annual return under section 92 are ordinarily kept at the registered office. They may be kept at another place in India where more than one-tenth of the Members entered in the register reside, if approved by special resolution at a general meeting. Subject to lawful closure and prescribed restrictions, the registers, indices and copies of returns are open for inspection during business hours. Members, debenture-holders, other security holders and beneficial owners have inspection rights without charge; other persons pay the prescribed fee. The categories identified in subsection (3) may take extracts without charge or require copies on payment of prescribed fees. Prescribed particulars are excluded under the applicable rules; verify the current rule text before relying on the precise list. If inspection, an extract or a copy is refused, subsection (4) provides a penalty of ₹1,000 for every day the refusal/default continues, subject to a maximum of ₹1,00,000, on the company and every officer in default. Under subsection (5), the Central Government may direct immediate inspection or allow the extract to be taken forthwith. This topic remains under source and current-law review.

sections.heading: Place of keeping
sections.body: Registers required under section 88 and copies of the annual return filed under section 92 are ordinarily kept at the registered office. They may be kept at another place in India where more than one-tenth of the Members entered in the register reside, if approved by a special resolution passed at a general meeting.

sections.heading: Inspection and fees
sections.body: Subject to lawful closure and applicable restrictions, the registers, indices and copies of returns are open for inspection during business hours. Members, debenture-holders, other security holders and beneficial owners may inspect without charge; other persons pay the prescribed fee.

sections.heading: Extracts, copies and prescribed exclusions
sections.body: The persons covered by subsection (3) may take extracts without charge or require copies on payment of prescribed fees. Prescribed particulars are excluded under the applicable rules. Check the current rules for the exact list of fields excluded from inspection, extracts and copies.

sections.heading: Penalty for refusal
sections.body: If inspection, an extract or a copy required under section 94 is refused, the company and every officer in default are liable to a penalty of ₹1,000 for every day during which the refusal/default continues, subject to a maximum of ₹1,00,000.

sections.heading: Immediate remedy
sections.body: The Central Government may by order direct immediate inspection of the document or direct that the required extract be allowed to be taken forthwith.

examples.title: Alternative place of keeping
examples.body: Check both conditions: the alternative place must be in India and more than one-tenth of the Members entered in the register must reside there; a special resolution at a general meeting must approve the arrangement.

hypotheticals.question: A company refuses a Member's inspection request for the register of members. What consequences may follow under section 94?
hypotheticals.analysis: Check whether the register is covered and whether the request is within the statutory inspection right. Subsection (4) imposes a penalty of ₹1,000 per day while refusal/default continues, capped at ₹1,00,000, on the company and every officer in default. Subsection (5) permits the Central Government to direct immediate inspection.

hypotheticals.question: May an ordinary member of the public obtain every field in the register of members?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Although section 94 permits inspection and copies subject to prescribed fees and rights, prescribed particulars such as addresses, email IDs, Unique Identification Numbers and PAN are excluded under the applicable rules. Check the current rules for the exact excluded fields.

distinctions.title: Inspection entitlement and copy entitlement
distinctions.left: Eligible holders may inspect covered registers and returns during business hours, with no fee for the listed holder categories.
distinctions.right: Copies may be requested on prescribed fees; prescribed personal particulars remain excluded.

rows.left: No fee for listed holder categories; other persons pay prescribed fee

misconceptions.trap: Assuming registers may be kept at any location once a special resolution is passed.
misconceptions.correction: The alternative location must be in India where more than one-tenth of the Members reside, and a special resolution must approve it.

misconceptions.trap: Treating all inspection/copy requests as free or allowing all personal fields to be disclosed.
misconceptions.correction: The fee and entitlement depend on the requester category, and prescribed particulars are excluded from inspection/extract/copy.

misconceptions.trap: Omitting the continuing daily penalty or the Central Government's immediate-inspection power.
misconceptions.correction: Subsections (4) and (5) state those separate consequences and remedies.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 94 principally regulate?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: The location of specified registers/annual-return copies, inspection and copy access, prescribed restrictions, the penalty for refusal and the Central Government's immediate-access remedy.
